questions.question_text: Two figures are similar. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
They are the same shape and the same size.
options.why: Same shape and same size describes congruent figures; similar figures need not be the same size.

options.text: Their corresponding sides are equal in length.
options.why: Equal corresponding sides is a congruence property; in similar figures the sides are in a common ratio, not necessarily equal.

options.text: Their corresponding angles are in the same ratio as their sides.
options.why: Angles are copied exactly in similar figures — only the sides are scaled by the common ratio.

questions.solution_text: Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size: corresponding angles are equal, and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.

options.text: Similar — every matching-side ratio equals $1.5$.
Not similar — the ratios of matching sides are different.
options.why: Pairing non-corresponding sides (such as $\frac{9}{5}=1.8$ and $\frac{6}{4}=1.5$) gives unequal ratios; matched correctly, $\frac{9}{6}=\frac{7.5}{5}=\frac{6}{4}=1.5$.

options.text: Not similar — the sides are not equal in length.
options.why: Equal sides are needed for congruence, not similarity; similar figures only need sides in one common ratio.

options.text: Not similar — one triangle is larger than the other.
options.why: A size difference never rules out similarity; similar figures are usually different sizes.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{9}{6}=1.5$
$\frac{7.5}{5}=1.5$
$\frac{6}{4}=1.5$
Matching angles are equal and every matching-side ratio is $1.5$, so the triangles are similar.

options.text: Not similar — $\frac{11}{5}=2.2$ but $\frac{8}{2}=4$.
Similar — both are rectangles, so all their angles match.
options.why: Equal angles alone are not enough; the matching sides must also be in the same ratio, and here they are not.

options.text: Similar — each side of the larger rectangle is $6$ cm longer.
options.why: Adding the same amount to each side is not the similarity test — the sides must be multiplied by the same number, and $2.2\neq4$.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{11}{5}=2.2$
$\frac{8}{2}=4$
The matching-side ratios are not equal, so the rectangles are not similar.

options.text: Similar — every matching-side ratio equals $2$.
Not similar — the sides increase by different amounts ($16-8=8$ but $6-3=3$).
options.why: Comparing by subtraction is the wrong test; similarity compares by division, and $\frac{16}{8}=\frac{6}{3}=\frac{10}{5}=2$.

options.text: Not similar — a pentagon has five sides, so five different ratios can never all agree.
options.why: The number of sides is irrelevant; here all five ratios equal the same value $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{16}{8}=2$
$\frac{6}{3}=2$
$\frac{10}{5}=2$
Matching angles are equal and every matching-side ratio is $2$, so the pentagons are similar.

questions.question_text: All the angles of one parallelogram are equal to the matching angles of another parallelogram. Must the two parallelograms be similar?

options.text: No — their matching sides may not be in the same ratio.
Yes — equal matching angles is what makes two figures similar.
options.why: Equal angles is only half the test for polygons; the matching sides must also be in one common ratio.

options.text: Yes — all parallelograms have the same shape.
options.why: Parallelograms can be long and thin or nearly square, so they do not all share one shape.

options.text: No — parallelograms of different sizes are never similar.
options.why: Different sizes never rule out similarity; the sides just need to be in the same ratio.

questions.solution_text:
Equal matching angles is only one of the two properties.
A $2\times6$ parallelogram and a $2\times3$ parallelogram with the same angles have $\frac{2}{2}=1$ but $\frac{6}{3}=2$, so they are not similar.
The sides must also be in the same ratio, so the answer is no.

questions.question_text: Which of these groups of figures are always similar to each other?

options.text: All equilateral triangles
All rectangles
options.why: All rectangles have equal angles, but their sides need not be in the same ratio — a long thin rectangle is not similar to a square-ish one.

options.text: All isosceles triangles
options.why: Isosceles triangles can have different angle sizes, so their matching angles need not be equal.

options.text: All rhombuses
options.why: Rhombuses have four equal sides but their angles vary — a squashed rhombus is not similar to a square-like one.

questions.solution_text:
Every equilateral triangle has three $60^{\circ}$ angles, and its three equal sides mean every matching-side ratio between two equilateral triangles is the same one number.
Equal angles and one common ratio, so all equilateral triangles are similar.

options.text: No — the third angles are $70^{\circ}$ and $75^{\circ}$, so the angle sets do not match.
Yes — both triangles contain an angle of $60^{\circ}$.
options.why: One equal pair of angles is not enough; every pair of matching angles must be equal, and the sets $50^{\circ},60^{\circ},70^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ},60^{\circ},75^{\circ}$ differ.

options.text: Yes — the third angles must be equal because both triangles have an angle sum of $180^{\circ}$.
options.why: The same total does not force the individual angles to match: $180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=70^{\circ}$ but $180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-45^{\circ}=75^{\circ}$.

options.text: No — the triangles are different sizes.
options.why: Size never decides similarity; the reason is that the matching angles cannot all be equal.

questions.solution_text:
$180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=70^{\circ}$, angle sum of a triangle
$180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}-45^{\circ}=75^{\circ}$, angle sum of a triangle
The angle sets are $50^{\circ},60^{\circ},70^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ},60^{\circ},75^{\circ}$, which do not match, so the matching angles cannot all be equal and the triangles cannot be similar.

options.text: Similar — $\frac{10}{4}$ and $\frac{15}{6}$ both equal $2.5$.
Not similar — the sides grow by different amounts ($10-4=6$ but $15-6=9$).
options.why: Similarity compares sides by division, not subtraction; both ratios equal $2.5$.

options.text: Not similar — $2.5$ is not a whole number, so the sides are not in a proper ratio.
options.why: A common ratio does not need to be a whole number; any one shared value, such as $2.5$, makes the sides proportional.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{10}{4}=2.5$
$\frac{15}{6}=2.5$
All angles are right angles and both matching-side ratios equal $2.5$, so the rectangles are similar.
